scope.description: Census of every Python example under /home/fedora/rk3588/examples and map of exercised RKNPU blocks to current FPGA RTL support.
scope.board_access: none; no ssh/scp, no submit, no FPGA program/flash
scope.source_edits: none; this directory is the only write target
scope.capture_rule: A case is called captured only when its result tree contains capture.json plus a real output BO (out.bin or output.bin). A manifest READY flag alone is prepared, not captured. Oracle PASS/FAIL is recorded separately.
scope.fpga_rule: RTL support is claimed only from actual rtl/ modules and docs, not from RK silicon behavior or prepared command streams.

status_vocabulary.captured_exact: At least one bundle case has a real device capture and an exact oracle comparison.
status_vocabulary.captured_tolerance: At least one bundle case has a real device capture and passes the declared tolerance, but is not byte-exact.
status_vocabulary.captured_known_divergence: At least one bundle case has a real device capture but differs from the declared oracle; the difference is known and scoped.
status_vocabulary.captured_truth_table: A real device capture exists as a truth table/characterization with no pass/fail oracle by design (currently fdiv-systematic).
status_vocabulary.captured_unverified: Real device output exists but no completed oracle comparison is available.
status_vocabulary.captured_not_implemented: A real device capture exists, but the corresponding arithmetic is not implemented in the FPGA RTL (currently FDIV).
status_vocabulary.prepared_not_run: Bundle is READY and runner-valid, but there is no results directory with real output BOs.
status_vocabulary.blocked_missing_abi: The example or bundle needs an ABI/transport the Rocket/FPGA path does not provide (vendor RKNPU, core_mask/subcore_task, PC self-address patch).
status_vocabulary.blocked_missing_rtl: A required arithmetic or data-movement block has no RTL implementation.
status_vocabulary.blocked_unsupported_dtype_shape: The dtype, shape, pad/stride/grouped contract, oracle or source evidence is unsupported or absent.
status_vocabulary.blocked_multitask_execution: The bundle needs a multi-task Rocket job, but this Rocket/FPGA path completes only the first task; the bundle is blocked or split into one-task cases.
status_vocabulary.blocked_bundle_integrity: Manifest says READY but the official runner validator rejects the bundle.
status_vocabulary.unknown: The example's semantics or output contract are not established.

block_support.label: DPU elementwise FP16 ALU
scope: Binary16 ADD, SUB, MUL, MAX; NEG is MUL by -1.
Eight lanes per group; width is count-minus-one in groups of eight, up to 7999.
Strict fixed profile: DPU pointer/mode/data-format, height=0, notch=0, channels=0x00070007, RDMA mode 0x00017849, OUT_CVT 0x00010001.
Round-to-nearest-even, gradual underflow, RK-captured NaN 0x7c01, signed-zero and SUB-infinity policy.
not_supported: FDIV (captured on RK, decoder rejects EW_CFG 0x108303c0).
INT8/INT16/INT32 EW, BS/BN arithmetic, LUT/activation, FP32 output, CAST_BOOL_HALF.
General surface strides, ERDMA broadcast, BRDMA/NRDMA, multi-input, runtime gather/layout repair.
evidence: build/rk3588-kernel-comparison-v1: real Rocket capture + RTL simulation for ADD/SUB/MUL/NEG/MAX at N=8.

build/rk3588-example-captures/results/ew-fp16-20261105T201400Z: 45/45 supported-op logical PASS; 9 FDIV captured, 7 exact, 2 A/7 cases (20 halfwords) explained by the three-guard-bit ties-to-even contract, matching 1452/1452 real lanes.

build/rk3588-example-captures/results/fdiv-systematic-20261105T204746Z: 8 cases, 512 bytes, 256 operand classes; the 32-lane finite sweep and 256-class truth table are correctly rounded nearest-even, with no pass/fail oracle by design.

block_support.label: DPU elementwise integer ALU
scope: RK examples exercise INT8/INT16/INT32 ADD/MIN/SUB/MUL/MAX, saturation and INT16->INT32 regrouping.

not_supported: No integer ALU exists. rk_fp16_alu.sv is half-precision only and rk_ew_regs.sv fixes DATA_FORMAT to 0x48000002.
No integer saturation, no EDATA_SIZE integer modes, no INT16->INT32 WDMA.
evidence: build/rk3588-example-captures/results/ew-int-20261105T200154Z: 15/15 submit_ret=0 and masked oracle PASS.
int16_add_to_int32_c8_w1 is a 31-QWORD bundle; one zero fetch-padding QWORD is needed only for generic-runner replay.

block_support.label: CMAC / CACC FP16 GEMM
scope: FP16 C32/K16, 512 parallel products, FP48 accumulation and FP32 finalization followed by FP16 output writes.
Strict terminal 49-QWORD profile: rows 1..2047, input/output channels multiples of 32, input channels >= output channels, no ReLU, no FP32 output, physical packed operands.
Framework full profile adds layout DMA and six compiler shapes; default EW board top does not instantiate the CMAC product path.
not_supported: No general GEMM ABI, no runtime gathers, no arbitrary K/N/M, no FP32 output, no activation, no INT8/INT4.
Not the default EW endpoint; requires the explicit RKCD/RKLY/RKRS framework profile.
evidence: docs/CMAC_PROFILE_CANDIDATE.md and docs/FRAMEWORK_FULL_PROFILE.md.
docs/CMAC_PRODUCT_PATH.md: the product leaf is not instantiated by the EW DMA/host/board top.

block_support.label: DPU batch/scale/norm and LUT stages
scope: RK examples exercise BS/BN ALU/MUL/ReLU/PReLU, BRDMA/NRDMA inputs, four-input sums, 513-entry LUTs.
rk_ew_regs.sv accepts BS_CFG/BN_CFG and related fields only at fixed no-op values as part of the all-or-none FP16 initialization group.
not_supported: No BS/BN add/mul/relu/prelu arithmetic, no BRDMA/NRDMA, no LUT, no nonzero EW scale/offset/shift.
Nonzero BS/BN values in conv_mesa/simple_conv/elementwise_int are rejected by the strict decoder.
evidence: rtl/rk_ew_regs.sv: fixed 0x53/0x00/0x02 init values and no arithmetic.
docs/REVIEW_AND_PLAN.md lists LUT/activation/conversion modes as deferred.

block_support.label: RDMA and PC command chain
scope: EW DMA fetches raw QWORDs from command memory, supports linked terminal EW tasks, next-address/amount tails and a task limit.
One outstanding halfword memory request; A/B/D scalar reads and writes; 16-byte aligned bases.
not_supported: General DPU RDMA: surface line strides, ERDMA per-channel broadcast, BRDMA/NRDMA, multi-surface, FP32 operands, bursts.
Vendor core_mask/subcore_task multi-core dispatch; CMAC linked PC chains (CMAC DMA is one terminal task).
evidence: docs/PC_DMA.md and rtl/rk_ew_dma.sv.
rtl/cmac/rk_cmac_array_dma.sv comments: one terminal task for the CMAC controller.

case_list.blocker: No source path encodes a convolution stride.  The FP16 shape parser accepts an sN field (expt/conv_simple.py:228-238), but _conv_params ignores it (lines 297-311) and make_regs always writes CNA_CONV_CON3 = (1<<3)|1 = 0x9, i.e. stride 1 (expt/conv_simple.py:408).  kernel_6_18/simple_conv.py hardcodes the same value at line 557.  Emitting a stride-2 case would require a new CNA_CONV_CON3 encoding that these sources do not provide.

No SAME-padding path exists in the named sources.  The FP16 make_regs() never writes CNA_PAD_CON0 or CNA_PAD_CON1 (expt/conv_simple.py:383-440) and _conv_params computes out_h/out_w = in_h/in_w - k + 1, i.e. valid-only (expt/conv_simple.py:301).  The INT8 builder writes CNA_PAD_CON0 = 0 (kernel_6_18/simple_conv.py:575), sets CNA_PAD_CON1 only to a zero-point fill value (line 584), and also computes valid-only output geometry (lines 81-82).  A SAME case would require new pad-register evidence and an output-with-halo contract that the sources do not provide.

This C8 shape cannot be packed safely with the FP16 builder.  For in_c=8, _conv_align_c returns 16 (expt/conv_simple.py:283-286), but _conv_input_pack_c2 returns 8 (lines 289-294).  pack_input() then writes c1*c2 = 8 channels per pixel (lines 364-374), while make_regs sets CNA_DATA_SIZE1 = ((in_c-1)<<16) | data_in_channel_aligned = 0x00070010, i.e. a 16-channel aligned field (lines 393,410).  The source's own known-supported table has no C8 entry (lines 207-217), and its validated small-channel path is the <=4-channel NHWC case (C3/C4, where use_nhwc is true and the CVT fields carry the real channel count).  There is no source-supported padding contract that fills the missing 8 channels for C8 (the same gap affects 5 <= in_c <= 8).  The READY small cases therefore use C4, and the larger cases use C16/C32 where the packed channel count equals the aligned count.

The grouped path cannot be expressed safely from these sources.  The FP16 make_regs() has no group-count register and its known-supported table has no grouped entry (expt/conv_simple.py:207-217,383-440).  The only grouped implementation is kernel_6_18/simple_conv.py::run_conv2d_grouped (lines 729-759), which slices input/weight/bias and calls run_conv2d_shape once per group; each call overwrites the shared BOs in write_buffers (lines 675-691) and does its own npu_submit (lines 871-872).  A single bundle would therefore need per-group BOs plus a multi-task PC chain, and the chain's PC_BASE_ADDRESS would have to be regcmd_addr + task_offset.  The bundle patch schema can only bind named buffer addresses, not the regcmd self-address, so the chain cannot be encoded without leaving an unpatched address.

All 26 READY conv cases are captured: conv-fp16 9/9 exact, conv-gemm-vendor 10/10 PASS (8 exact, 2 tolerance), and conv-simple 4/7 exact plus 3 known divergences. The 13 BLOCKED cases are 3 vendor-ABI, 3 multi-task and 7 other shape/source. None can execute on the FPGA.

top_gaps.why: FDIV is captured in 9 ew-fp16 cases and the 8-case, 256-class fdiv-systematic truth table. The 32-lane finite sweep and the 256-class truth table are correctly rounded nearest-even. The EW FP16 A/7 cases fdiv_p1_n33 and fdiv_p1_n1024 are the known divergence: 20 halfwords differ, explained by the three-guard-bit ties-to-even contract, which matches 1452/1452 real lanes.
